label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Thursday's launch (Inês)

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family in the Netherlands. I am taking the train tonight and I don't know yet how long I will be away. So Thursday is yours. I'm sorry to leave you with this, and especially sorry about the timing, because I found a real error this afternoon and it's not fixed everywhere yet.

Before the list, I want to say this properly. I trust you completely with this launch. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, so you know the part Kessler will go after better than anyone in the room. And remember Lisbon. When the projector died at the COP side event you carried my panel without slides and nobody noticed anything was wrong. You are better live than you think.

Everything below is in this folder or in my inbox. I've put it in the order I would do it.

1. THE FIGURE 3 ERROR (most urgent)

My note "ERROR figure 3" in this folder has the details. In short: figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, where the free allocation phase-out was not applied. The correct 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper doesn't change, but the headline number does.

Where it stands:
- PDF v7 on the drive is corrected (pages 3, 14, 15). Use v7 for anything that goes out from now on.
- Deck v4 is NOT corrected. Slides 6 and 9 still say 2.1. Slide 9 is the revenue chart.
- The press release is NOT corrected. Hanna sent it under embargo to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday and it says 2.1. The embargo lifts Thursday 10:00 CET.

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, say so plainly: "Marieke used an estimate from an earlier model run, it was caught before publication, the correct figure is 1.4 billion and the conclusions stand." You don't need to protect me on this.

2. PRESS RELEASE CORRECTION (tomorrow, Tuesday)

Please sit down with Hanna tomorrow morning and get a corrected release to the same 34 contacts, ideally Tuesday and definitely well before the embargo lifts. A short cover note is enough: "Correction to the embargoed release of 20 November: the 2030 figure should read EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Embargo unchanged, Thursday 26 November 10:00 CET. Updated report attached." Attach PDF v7.

If Hanna wants a senior name on the correction, Geert can sign it off. He knows I'm away. Don't wait for me on this one.

3. FIX THE DECK

Correct slides 6 and 9 in deck v4 to 1.4 and save it as v5, so nobody opens the old one by mistake. Check the speaker notes as well, I think 2.1 is in there too. While you're in there, see point 4: the presentation is now 15 minutes, not 20, so cut whatever you want. It's your talk now. Present it your way and don't try to give mine.

4. REPLY TO TOMÁS (by Wednesday 12:00 at the latest)

Tomás (Lindqvist's office) emailed this morning with changes. It's in my inbox, "Thursday - small change to timings":
- The MEP has a vote moved into Thursday lunchtime and has to leave at 13:30.
- Presentation 15 min instead of 20.
- Panel starts at 12:50 instead of 12:55.
- She wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves.
- He needs final badge names from our side by Wednesday 12:00, or security won't let them in.

Please reply to him and:
- tell him I can't attend and that you will present and sit on the panel in my place
- confirm the new timings
- send him your name for a badge (and Hanna's, or anyone else from us who is coming), and take my name off
- ask who moderates after 13:30 when Lindqvist leaves. The run of show has her moderating until 14:00, so that gap needs a name. If he has nobody, you could suggest you take over the Q&A from the panel, or ask whether someone from her office can step in.

The updated run of show then looks like this: guests at the security entrance by 12:00 (Tomás collects badges), lunch outside the room from 12:00, 12:30 welcome Lindqvist, 12:35 presentation (15 min), 12:50 panel with Abena (remote), Kessler and you, Lindqvist takes her questions before 13:30, close at 14:00.

5. PRESS CALLS (Wednesday afternoon)

Hanna told two journalists I'd be available on Wednesday afternoon. One is from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. They're in the calendar at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each by phone, and Hanna still has to confirm. Please do them instead of me. Hanna can tell them it's you, the lead co-author. Both have the release with 2.1 in it, so start with the correction rather than waiting for them to notice. If you say it first, it's a non-story.

6. ABENA

The remote link is in the calendar invite. She tested it last week and it worked. A short email to her on Wednesday would be good: say I'm away for family reasons, that you're on the panel, and give her the corrected figure so she doesn't quote 2.1. She was strong on our call about the LDC side and I expect she'll back the paper there.

7. KESSLER

He'll try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through. Don't let him set the tone. Acknowledge it, answer it, and then bring it back to the actual question of the paper, which is who pays and where the revenue goes.

My reply lines are in "Reply lines for Kessler" in this folder, but you know this better than I do:
- 80% is the central case. Annex B runs 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly. Being open about the 40% case is our strength, not a weakness. Don't get defensive.
- On resource shuffling: we agree it's a risk, we cover it in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.
- His written comments (in this folder) say his members report much lower pass-through for small manufacturers. If he brings anecdotes, you can say we'd welcome the data and would happily run it.

He may also use the correction. If he does, the line is the same as in point 1: an earlier run, caught before publication, conclusions unchanged. Then move on.

8. AFTER THE EVENT

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is coming with a colleague. For their grant report she needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please ask someone to take photos (Hanna, or someone from Tomás's side), and count heads or get the list from Tomás. You could say hello to her on Thursday and tell her I'm sorry to miss it. She congratulated both of us on the paper, by the way, so the thanks are yours as much as mine.

CALLING ME

You can call me. Tomorrow before 9 is the best time. After 9 I might not pick up, and I don't know what the rest of the week will look like. If you can't reach me, decide yourself. You don't need my approval for any of this. For anything that needs a senior name, go to Geert.

QUICK CHECKLIST

Tuesday:
- corrected release with Hanna, Geert signs off if needed
- deck v5 with slides 6 and 9 fixed and cut to 15 minutes
- reply to Tomás: you replace me, timings, badges, moderator after 13:30

Wednesday:
- badge names to Tomás by 12:00
- email to Abena with the corrected figure
- press calls at 14:00 and 15:00

Thursday:
- embargo lifts 10:00
- at the Spinelli building by 12:00
- presentation 12:35
- panel 12:50

By 4 December:
- photos and attendance numbers to Lucy

Again, I'm sorry for the mess. The paper is good and so are you. I'm not worried about Thursday, only sorry I won't be there to see it.

Marieke
